stem: An assistant retrieves documents on behalf of a user. What is the correct way to prevent it exposing documents that user is not entitled to see?

options.text: Filter the retrieved results at query time using the end user's permissions (or the user's identity propagated to the data source)
Tell the model not to reveal restricted documents
Index only documents everyone may see and ignore the rest
Rely on the user to ask only for permitted content

explanation: Authorisation must be enforced by the system on the retrieval path, using the real user's identity. A prompt instruction is not an access control. Indexing only public content is safe but may not meet the use case.

stem: Which practice best supports data minimisation when sending text to a hosted model?

options.text: Send complete customer records so the model has full context
Send only the fields needed for the task, redact or tokenise identifiers where possible, and log what was sent
Disable all logging
Send data in uppercase

explanation: Minimise what leaves your boundary, mask what the task does not need, and keep an audit trail of what was shared.

stem: "On-behalf-of" identity propagation for an agent means:

options.text: The agent uses its own all-powerful service account for every action
The agent calls downstream systems with a token that represents the end user (and the agent), so the downstream system applies the user's permissions
The user shares their password with the agent
The agent never calls downstream systems

explanation: Propagating the user context lets downstream systems enforce existing authorisation and produce attributable audit trails. Shared passwords and super-user accounts break both.

stem: An HR assistant answers questions from policy documents and from employee records. In testing, a junior employee obtained another employee's salary band by asking cleverly.
constraints: Records system already enforces role-based access
Assistant uses one service account to read records
Audit requires knowing who saw what

options.text: Replace the service account with propagated user identity so the records system enforces the user's permissions, filter retrieval by entitlements, and log the user identity with each access.
Add a prompt rule not to reveal salaries to junior staff.
Keep the service account but only allow questions from managers.
Hide the records tool and answer only from policies.

rationales.text: Existing access control in the records system should decide, using the real user identity.
A prompt rule is a sufficient access control.
Per-user audit logs need the user identity at the point of access.
A shared service account preserves per-user audit.

explanation: The flaw is architectural: a privileged service account lets the model act with more authority than the user has. Propagating identity makes the authoritative system decide and keeps audit meaningful.
model_answer: Use on-behalf-of tokens or equivalent, rely on the records system's access rules, filter retrieval by entitlement, and keep per-user logs; avoid giving the model privileged standing access.

rubric.criterion: Identifies privileged service account as root cause

stem: A European client wants to use a hosted model API for summarising support tickets that contain names, email addresses and sometimes health details.
constraints: Some tickets may contain special-category data

options.text: Assess lawful basis and a data-processing agreement, minimise and redact before sending, choose a region and retention settings that meet policy, exclude special-category tickets unless explicitly covered, and record the decision.
Send everything and rely on the provider's general privacy page.
Refuse all hosted models permanently.
Remove only email addresses and send the rest.

rationales.text: Legal basis, contract and data location are architectural inputs, not afterthoughts.
Provider marketing statements replace a contract.
Redaction and exclusion reduce what is exposed.
Removing one identifier type is enough for health data.

explanation: Personal and special-category data call for explicit legal and technical controls: contract, minimisation, location and retention. Blanket refusal is safe but ignores options such as redaction and private deployment. This is educational, not legal advice.
model_answer: Confirm lawful basis and a processing agreement, minimise and redact, pick region and retention, exclude or separately handle special-category content, and document the decision for review with legal counsel.
